findings.summary: CODEX-03-B adds migration 004, a synthetic entitlement kernel that leaves commit and rollback to the caller, and real-PGlite tests. The kernel does what the card asks. It uses the existing local-synthetic guard, sets its own savepoint before any write (an autocommit caller gets the database's 25P01 error) and locks in architecture order: household, current consent, request, grant, period, claim, then publication and assignment. Trials start only on an explicit call and never restart; the stored digest makes repeat calls safe and changed ones conflict. Hold eligibility uses the stored original receipt time and allowance is enforced under the period lock. Reserve and consume still work after expiry, pre-ready release frees the unit, and consumed or released claims cannot reopen. Consume requires a scoped assignment binding. Every result is marked uncommitted:true, and no durability flag, price, offer or receipt claim is invented. The controller ran the tests, the build and the protected checker against the reviewed tree, and all three exited 0. The checker includes the protected entitlement_probe.mjs, which I read. It covers the scenarios the coder's own test file leaves out, such as late reserve/consume, consume binding, child allocation and source correction. The open policy gates (G-E03/G-E04, journals, durability, RLS, multi-host races) are preserved. The remaining findings are minor.

findings.title: App test file omits several card-listed scenarios; coverage relies on probe
findings.problem: The card says 'Actual app tests must exercise ... wrong scopes/epochs, late reserve/consume, release/correction, child allocation and consume binding/idempotence.' The repository's own tests cover activation and non-activation, last-unit serialization, release, rollback and savepoint recovery, receipt boundaries and withdrawn consent. They do not cover child allocation, consume binding or idempotence, late reserve/consume, source correction, or wrong-household and epoch-mismatch denial. Those scenarios are exercised only by the protected controller probe (.codex/tools/entitlement_probe.mjs). That probe ran and passed on this tree, so the evidence exists, but it is not in the app's own `npm test` regression suite.
findings.fix_check: tests/loop-entitlements.test.mjs (or a sibling app test) includes real-PGlite cases for child-scope allocation and denial, consume with a valid binding, a wrong-household binding and an exact replay, reserve/consume after trial_end, a request_source_scopes successor that cannot mint a second claim, and an epoch-mismatch denial. `npm test` passes with those cases included.

findings.title: Activation digest includes scope; replay after epoch change conflicts
findings.problem: digest({kind:'activate', scope:trustedScope, ...}) includes consent_epoch in the digest. After a legitimate move to a new active epoch, replaying the same activation command_id returns 'conflict' instead of the stored original result. This is safe (it never mints or restarts a trial) but may surprise WM04/WM08 integrators who expect exact replay.
findings.fix_check: Either document that the consent epoch is part of command identity, or digest only household_id plus the command and policy. A test should show the chosen behavior.

findings.title: Same-transaction concurrency guard is object-identity only
findings.problem: The busy WeakSet only catches concurrent calls on the same tx object. A wrapper or proxy around the same transaction bypasses it. The code comment and REPORT document this as a caller obligation, which the card permits ('No concurrent kernel methods in the same caller transaction').
findings.fix_check: The WM04/WM08 integration owners keep this documented caller obligation; no change needed in this card.
